voiceover: Jesus' favourite name for himself was 'Son of Man.' It appears about eighty times in the Gospels, almost always on his own lips. And it sounds humble — just 'a human being.' But the background is Daniel chapter seven. There the prophet sees 'one like a son of man, coming with the clouds of heaven.' He approaches the Ancient of Days and receives a kingdom that never ends. And 'coming with the clouds' is imagery the Hebrew Bible uses of God's own appearing. So at his trial, Jesus fuses Daniel seven with Psalm one hundred and ten, and claims to be the heavenly figure enthroned beside God. Then there is 'Lord.' Kyrios — the word the New Testament writers use to render God's own name from the Hebrew Scriptures. And Paul writes: if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe God raised him, you will be saved — for everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. He's quoting a line about calling on the name of God. Read together, these names place Jesus inside what Israel reserved for her God alone.

It appears about eighty times in the Gospels, almost always on his own lips. And it sounds humble — just 'a human being.'
But the background is Daniel chapter seven. There the prophet sees 'one like a son of man, coming with the clouds of heaven.'
He approaches the Ancient of Days and receives a kingdom that never ends. And 'coming with the clouds' is imagery the Hebrew Bible uses of God's own appearing.
So at his trial, Jesus fuses Daniel seven with Psalm one hundred and ten, and claims to be the heavenly figure enthroned beside God.
Then there is 'Lord.' Kyrios — the word the New Testament writers use to render God's own name from the Hebrew Scriptures.

And Paul writes: if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe God raised him, you will be saved — for everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. He's quoting a line about calling on the name of God.
Read together, these names place Jesus inside what Israel reserved for her God alone.
